summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease, diabetes, coronary artery disease with prior CABG and stents, peripheral vascular disease, and a pacemaker was admitted for chest pressure and fever. Workup revealed enterococcal bacteremia, and a transesophageal echocardiogram confirmed endocarditis with a vegetation on the pacemaker lead. The infected device was surgically removed, and the patient was started on a six-week course of IV vancomycin and gentamicin administered during hemodialysis. Blood cultures cleared, and the patient improved clinically, with resolution of fever and chest pain. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for infectious disease follow-up, wound care, and continuation of antibiotics through dialysis access.
problems: Diabetes with renal and neurological manifestations
